To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we identified 3,816 genes whose expression was significantly affected by 6,500 single nucleotide polymorphisms in the whole blood of Korean patients with Crohn’s disease, and we identified two potential target genes, TNFRSF15 and GPR 35, at two loci previously reported as Crohn’s disease susceptibility loci.

eQTL analyses of CD in Korean patients with CD identified 3,816 differentially expressed genes and that integrated analyses of CD GWAS data and eQTL data revealed two putative causal genes, TNFSFR15 and GPR 35, at two CD susceptibility loci.

we have identified a number of novel disease-associated genes and pathways that are relevant to Crohn’s disease pathogenesis, and that our findings have important implications for understanding disease pathophysiology.
